questions.stem:
84M w/ nonvalvular AF, starting anticoagulation. h/o HTN.

Weight 72 kg
Cr 141 µmol/L (eGFR 42)

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.label: D

options.label: E
options.text: 10 mg BID x7d, then 5 mg BID
options.explanation: This is the VTE treatment regimen, not AF.

questions.explanation: Reduce apixaban to 2.5 mg BID in AF only when ≥2 of these are present: age ≥80, weight ≤60 kg, Cr ≥133 µmol/L. He has two (age and Cr). Off-label dose reduction for age or eGFR alone is common and may leave patients underprotected against stroke.

questions.stem:
62M w/ HFrEF (LVEF 30%), NYHA II, euvolemic. No DM. On sacubitril-valsartan, bisoprolol and spironolactone at tolerated doses.

BP 112/70, HR 64.
K 4.6 mmol/L
eGFR 52

options.label: A
options.explanation: Not one of the four foundational HFrEF therapies.

options.label: B
options.explanation: For sinus HR ≥70 despite a maximally tolerated beta-blocker; HR is 64.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Mainly an alternative when RAAS inhibitors can't be used.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Correct: SGLT2i is the fourth pillar, with or without diabetes.

options.label: E
options.explanation: No HF benefit, and BP is already low-normal.

questions.explanation: SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin) are one of the four foundational HFrEF therapies and reduce CV death and HF hospitalization whether or not the patient has diabetes. They need no titration and shouldn't wait until other drugs reach target doses. CCS advises against starting them at eGFR <20.

references.supports: SGLT2i in HFrEF with or without diabetes; not for eGFR <20

source.book: CCS/CHFS Heart Failure Guidelines (2022 cardiorenal update)

issues: Option B explanation is inaccurate: ivabradine's threshold is sinus HR ≥70 on a maximally tolerated beta-blocker, not 'tachycardia'.

questions.stem:
34M w/ 3d of sharp pleuritic chest pain, better sitting forward. Recent viral URI.

T 37.6, HR 96, BP 124/78.
ECG: diffuse ST elevation, PR depression
Troponin normal
TTE: small effusion, normal LV function

options.label: A
options.explanation: Correct: colchicine added to an NSAID reduces recurrence.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Treats pain, but recurrence is higher without colchicine.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Second-line; steroids are linked to more recurrence.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A small effusion without tamponade doesn't need drainage.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Colchicine is an adjunct to an NSAID, given for 3 months.

questions.explanation: Acute viral/idiopathic pericarditis is treated with high-dose ASA or an NSAID (e.g., ibuprofen 600 mg q8h for 1–2 weeks, with gastroprotection) plus colchicine for 3 months, which reduces recurrence. Corticosteroids are second-line, for contraindications or incomplete response, because they're associated with more recurrences.

references.supports: Colchicine reduces recurrence; glucocorticoids second-line

Untreated symptomatic severe AS has a poor prognosis, and exercise testing is contraindicated once symptoms are present.

questions.stem:
68M w/ COPD (FEV1 38% predicted), stable 6 wk after an exacerbation.

Room-air ABG: pH 7.40, PaCO2 46 mmHg, PaO2 57 mmHg
Hct 0.47
No edema; JVP normal; ECG normal
questions.lead: Most appropriate decision about home oxygen?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Needs PaO2 ≤55, or 56–59 with cor pulmonale or polycythemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Isolated nocturnal O2 hasn't been shown to improve survival here.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Correct: PaO2 57 without end-organ effects doesn't qualify.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Overtreatment risks worsening hypercapnia in COPD.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Not indicated on these resting results alone.

questions.explanation: LTOT improves survival in stable COPD when resting PaO2 is ≤55 mmHg (SpO2 ≤88%), or 56–59 mmHg with cor pulmonale, peripheral edema or polycythemia (Hct >55%). At PaO2 57 mmHg with none of these, he doesn't meet criteria, so reassess over time.

questions.stem:
72F w/ 2d of mild pleuritic chest pain. No hemoptysis, leg swelling, recent surgery or cancer.

HR 88, BP 136/80, SpO2 96% RA.
Wells: PE unlikely
D-dimer 640 µg/L FEU (lab cutoff 500)

options.label: A
options.explanation: Unneeded: D-dimer is below her age-adjusted cutoff.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Correct: her age-adjusted cutoff is 720 µg/L (72 × 10).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Imaging is unnecessary once PE is excluded by D-dimer.

options.label: D
options.explanation: PE is excluded; this adds only bleeding risk.

options.label: E
options.explanation: No DVT signs, and PE is already excluded.

questions.explanation: In patients >50 with non-high pretest probability, use an age-adjusted D-dimer cutoff of age × 10 µg/L. In ADJUST-PE, PE was safely excluded below this threshold (3-month VTE rate 0.3%), sparing many older patients CT. The formula assumes an assay reported in FEU with a 500 µg/L cutoff.

references.title: Age-adjusted D-dimer cutoff levels to rule out PE: ADJUST-PE (ACC journal scan)
references.supports: Age × 10 cutoff in ≥50; failure rate 0.3%

references.title: Age-adjusted D-dimer to exclude PE (Washington University EM)
references.supports: Formula assumes FEU assay with 500 µg/L cutoff

questions.stem:
66M w/ new right pleural effusion. Diagnostic thoracentesis:

Pleural protein 28 g/L; serum protein 70 g/L
Pleural LDH 190 U/L; serum LDH 210 U/L
Serum LDH upper limit of normal 250 U/L

options.label: A
options.explanation: One criterion is enough, and the LDH criteria are met.

options.label: B
options.text: Transudate: pleural LDH is below serum LDH
options.explanation: Not a Light's criterion; the LDH ratio of 0.90 exceeds 0.6.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Not needed; the effusion already meets exudate criteria.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The protein ratio is 0.40, below 0.5.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Correct: LDH ratio 0.90, and pleural LDH > two-thirds of the ULN.

questions.explanation: Light's criteria call an effusion exudative if ANY one is met: protein ratio >0.5, LDH ratio >0.6, or pleural LDH >2/3 of the serum ULN. Here both LDH criteria are met despite a protein ratio of 0.40. The criteria are about 98% sensitive for exudates, so false exudates (e.g., diuresed HF) are the main pitfall.

references.title: Light's criteria table, McMaster Textbook of Internal Medicine
references.supports: Criteria, ≥1 needed; sensitivity 98%, specificity 83%

references.title: Light's Criteria for Exudative Effusions (MDCalc)
references.supports: At least one criterion defines an exudate

questions.topic: Outpatient CAP in a healthy adult
questions.stem:
38M w/ 3d of fever and productive cough. No comorbidities, no recent Abx or hospitalization.

T 38.4, HR 98, RR 20, BP 124/76, SpO2 95% RA.
CXR: RLL consolidation
CURB-65: 0

options.label: A
options.explanation: Correct: first-line for healthy outpatients (strong recommendation).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Reserved for outpatients with comorbidities or beta-lactam issues.

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.explanation: Parenteral therapy is unnecessary for a low-risk outpatient.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Poor pneumococcal coverage; not a respiratory fluoroquinolone.

questions.explanation: For healthy outpatients without comorbidities or resistance risk factors, ATS/IDSA recommends amoxicillin 1 g TID; doxycycline is an alternative, and macrolide monotherapy only where pneumococcal macrolide resistance is <25%. Routine sputum and blood cultures aren't needed in outpatients.

references.title: ATS/IDSA publishes clinical guideline on community acquired pneumonia (ATS release, EurekAlert)
references.supports: Amoxicillin 1 g TID for healthy outpatients; combination for comorbidities; no routine cultures

questions.stem:
71M w/ known squamous cell lung cancer, 4d of confusion, polyuria and constipation.

BP 104/62, HR 108; dry mucous membranes.
Corrected Ca 3.7 mmol/L
Cr 165 µmol/L (baseline 90)
PTH suppressed

options.label: A
options.explanation: Not routine; consider only for volume overload after rehydration.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Useful for vitamin D–mediated causes, not this one.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Targets PTH-mediated disease; PTH is suppressed.

options.label: D
options.text: IV normal saline bolus, then infusion
options.explanation: Correct: correct volume depletion and promote calciuresis first.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Reserved for very severe or refractory cases.

questions.explanation: Severe hypercalcemia causes volume depletion, so start with isotonic saline (bolus, then infusion targeting urine output of 100–150 mL/h). Then give an antiresorptive, usually IV zoledronic acid adjusted for renal function, ± calcitonin as a rapid bridge, since bisphosphonates take 2–3 days to act.

references.title: Treatment of hypercalcemia of malignancy (Endocrinol Metab Clin N Am review)

questions.stem:
63M w/ T2DM x8y and MI 2y ago. On metformin, ASA, atorvastatin, ramipril and bisoprolol.

BMI 31
HbA1c 6.8%
eGFR 78

options.label: A
options.text: No change; HbA1c is at target
options.explanation: Cardiorenal-protective agents can be used in ASCVD even at target.

options.label: B
options.explanation: No proven CV benefit; adds hypoglycemia and weight gain.

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.explanation: DPP-4 inhibitors are CV-neutral.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Not needed at this HbA1c, with no CV benefit.

questions.explanation: Diabetes Canada (2020 update) advises that people with ASCVD, heart failure or CKD can receive a GLP-1 RA or SGLT2 inhibitor with proven cardiorenal benefit even when A1C is at target, by addition or substitution. Empagliflozin, or a GLP-1 RA such as semaglutide, would both fit here.

questions.topic: Upper GI bleed: timing of endoscopy
questions.stem:
61M w/ melena x1d. On naproxen for OA.

After 2 L crystalloid: BP 118/72, HR 92.
Hb 96 g/L
Glasgow-Blatchford score 9
IV pantoprazole started

options.label: A
options.explanation: Not required once he's been resuscitated and is stable.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Correct: consensus timing for acute upper GI bleeding.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Too late for a high-risk upper GI bleed.

options.label: D
options.explanation: He needs endoscopy for diagnosis and hemostasis.

options.label: E
options.explanation: PPI doesn't replace early endoscopy.

questions.explanation: The International Consensus Group (Barkun et al., 2019) suggests endoscopy within 24 hours of presentation for acute upper GI bleeding, after resuscitation. The same guideline suggests transfusing at Hb <80 g/L in patients without cardiovascular disease, with a higher threshold for those with it.

56M w/ alcohol-related cirrhosis and ascites p/w abdominal discomfort and new confusion.

T 37.9, BP 108/64.
Cr 128 µmol/L (baseline 80)
Bili 70 µmol/L
Ascitic fluid: neutrophils 0.6 × 10⁹/L; Gram stain negative

options.label: A
options.explanation: Right antibiotic, but omits albumin.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Doesn't treat the infection.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Used for SBP prophylaxis, not active infection.

options.label: D
options.text: Repeat paracentesis in 48 h, then treat
options.explanation: Neutrophils >0.25 × 10⁹/L already diagnose SBP; treat now.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Correct: albumin 1.5 g/kg on day 1 and 1 g/kg on day 3.

questions.explanation: Ascitic neutrophils >0.25 × 10⁹/L diagnose SBP. Treat with IV ceftriaxone or cefotaxime for at least 5 days, plus albumin 1.5 g/kg on day 1 and 1 g/kg on day 3, which lowers the risk of hepatorenal syndrome and improves survival. Hold nonselective beta-blockers if MAP <65.

GCS 13, BP 168/92.
CT head: right intracerebral hemorrhage
Cr 98 µmol/L

options.label: B

options.label: D

options.label: E

questions.explanation: Idarucizumab is a monoclonal antibody fragment that binds dabigatran with about 350 times its affinity for thrombin, reversing it within minutes. Thrombosis Canada recommends it for severe or life-threatening bleeding, or urgent surgery, in patients taking dabigatran.

questions.stem: 46M had a proximal DVT 3 wk after elective total knee arthroplasty. Treated with apixaban for 3 mo; now asymptomatic. No prior VTE, cancer or family history of VTE.

options.label: A
options.explanation: ASH suggests against it after surgery-provoked VTE.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Recurrence risk is low after a transient major risk factor.

options.label: C
options.text: Switch to apixaban 2.5 mg BID indefinitely
options.explanation: Extended therapy isn't needed after transient-provoked VTE.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Correct: 3-month primary treatment is complete.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Not indicated after a transient-provoked VTE.

questions.explanation: VTE provoked by a major transient risk factor such as surgery is treated for a primary course of about 3 months and then stopped, because recurrence risk is low. ASH suggests not testing for thrombophilia to decide duration in surgery-provoked VTE. Unprovoked VTE, by contrast, usually warrants indefinite therapy if bleeding risk allows.

67F on day 6 of ceftriaxone for pyelonephritis develops 5 watery stools/d.

T 37.8, BP 128/74.
WBC 12.4 × 10⁹/L
Cr 84 µmol/L
C. difficile toxin: positive

options.label: A
options.explanation: Only if fidaxomicin and oral vancomycin are unavailable.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Only an adjunct in fulminant CDI.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Correct: preferred by IDSA/SHEA 2021 for an initial episode.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Doesn't reach the colonic lumen.

options.label: E

Metronidazole is used only if neither is available. This episode is non-severe (WBC <15 × 10⁹/L, Cr <133 µmol/L).

questions.topic: Empiric therapy for bacterial meningitis over 50
questions.stem:
68M w/ 1d of fever, headache, neck stiffness and confusion. No focal deficits or papilledema. Blood cultures drawn.

T 39.2, HR 112, BP 128/70.
GCS 13

options.label: A
options.explanation: Misses Listeria, a concern after age 50.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Correct: covers Listeria; steroid with first dose.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Omits vancomycin for possible resistant pneumococcus.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Omits dexamethasone, which reduces mortality in pneumococcal meningitis.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Not the standard empiric regimen for community-acquired meningitis.

questions.explanation: Adults >50 need ampicillin added to vancomycin + ceftriaxone to cover Listeria. Give dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg (max 10 mg) IV q6h, starting before or with the first antibiotic dose. Never delay antibiotics for CT or LP, and with confusion add empiric acyclovir if HSV encephalitis is possible.

questions.stem:
66M w/ sudden right hemiparesis and aphasia; last known well 2.5 h ago. No anticoagulants.

BP 172/94, glucose 7.1 mmol/L.
NIHSS 12
Non-contrast CT: no hemorrhage

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.label: D

options.explanation: Delays treatment; CT excluding hemorrhage is enough.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Correct: eligible, disabling stroke within 4.5 h.

questions.explanation: Eligible patients with disabling ischemic stroke within 4.5 h of last known well should receive IV thrombolysis. Canadian Stroke Best Practices (2022) endorse tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg) as an alternative to alteplase, based largely on the Canadian AcT trial. With aphasia and NIHSS 12, also screen urgently for thrombectomy.

questions.stem:
45F w/ epilepsy has a generalized tonic-clonic seizure lasting 12 min. She has received lorazepam 4 mg IV twice, 5 min apart, and is still seizing.

Glucose 6.2 mmol/L
SpO2 94% on O2

options.label: A
options.explanation: Correct: a second-line agent after adequate benzodiazepines.

options.label: B
options.explanation: More benzodiazepine adds respiratory depression with less benefit.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Third-line, after a second-line agent fails.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Treats eclamptic seizures, not epilepsy-related status.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Seizures beyond 5 min need escalation.

questions.explanation: When status persists after adequate benzodiazepine dosing, give one second-line agent: levetiracetam, fosphenytoin or valproate, which were equally effective in ESETT (about 50% seizure cessation). Levetiracetam is often preferred for rapid infusion and few interactions. If seizures continue, move to anesthetic infusions.

questions.stem:
72M w/ CKD on ramipril and spironolactone p/w weakness.

HR 52, BP 118/70.
K 7.1 mmol/L (non-hemolyzed)
ECG: peaked T waves, wide QRS

options.label: A
options.explanation: Needed next, after membrane stabilization.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mainly for coexisting acidosis; doesn't stabilize the myocardium.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Removes K over hours; too slow as the first step.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Correct: stabilizes the cardiac membrane within minutes.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Definitive, but takes time to arrange; stabilize first.

questions.explanation: With ECG changes, give IV calcium first: it stabilizes the cardiac membrane within minutes but doesn't lower K, and may need repeating if ECG changes persist. Then shift K into cells (insulin with dextrose, salbutamol) and remove it (binders, diuretics or dialysis). Stop the ramipril and spironolactone.

ESR 88 mm/h
CRP 64 mg/L
Tender temporal artery w/ reduced pulse

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.explanation: A PMR-level dose; far too low for GCA.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A steroid-sparing add-on, not initial monotherapy.

questions.explanation: Suspected GCA with visual symptoms is an emergency: start IV pulse methylprednisolone immediately (ACR/VF 2021 favours IV pulse when vision is threatened), then high-dose oral prednisone. Arrange temporal artery biopsy, ideally within 2 weeks of starting steroids, and urgent ophthalmology review.
